name: memory-retrieval-v1-seed
description: Seed query set for Week3 Task3B. It evaluates focused memory retrieval over the Task3A synthetic learner DB and manifest.

cases.userQuestion: My Longest Substring code still fails on abba; have I made a left-boundary mistake like this before?
cases.notes: Direct same-problem review-debug query; should retrieve the active sliding-window mistake/weakness and failed review episode.

cases.userQuestion: When I use a sliding window with last_seen, what past window-shrink mistake should I watch for?
cases.notes: History/practice profile should recall active sliding-window mistakes.
limitations: Only one sliding-window problem exists in v1.

cases.userQuestion: For Two Sum, do I have a useful complement lookup pattern from previous practice?
cases.notes: Concept profile includes skill facts; the superseded same-index reuse fact should not surface as current.
limitations: Episode retrieval depends on FTS token overlap with the repair summary.

cases.userQuestion: If I am solving Two Sum again, should my old same-index reuse mistake still count as my current blocker?
cases.notes: The old episode can be relevant as history, but the contradicted fact should not be surfaced as current.
limitations: Fact recall denominator excludes this query because expectedFactKeys is empty.

cases.userQuestion: What binary-search invariant did I learn for insertion point, especially first >= target?
cases.notes: Should prefer the current skill over resolved/contradicted binary-search facts.
limitations: Current concept_chat profile can retrieve skill facts but only one episode.

cases.userQuestion: Have I previously returned left + 1 or misunderstood what left means after binary search?
cases.notes: History profile may include resolved facts as historical context; these stale facts are neutral here rather than forbidden.
limitations: Expected facts are intentionally empty because all binary-search mistake facts in v1 are non-current.

cases.userQuestion: I am confused again: when did I ask about Python dict.get versus checking if a key is in the dict?
cases.notes: This is expected to expose the current tag-match limitation: python_dict_get does not match Two Sum problem tags.
limitations: The fact is current in manifest but may be structurally hard to recall through current problem-tag scoring.

cases.userQuestion: How do I prefer explanations: short hints or long full solutions?
cases.notes: L2 preference facts are not expected positives because current retrieval profiles do not include factType=preference; profile output preferences are tracked diagnostically.
limitations: Preference fact recall is not counted in planted-fact recall for v1.

cases.userQuestion: Before giving a long binary-search explanation, do I prefer one concrete next step first?
cases.notes: Preference is represented through profile output preferences and the chat episode, not L2 preference retrieval.
limitations: The chat episode is tied to Two Sum, so FTS may or may not retrieve it from a binary-search prompt.

cases.userQuestion: Can I reuse my HashMap habit from Two Sum when thinking about last_seen in a string problem?
cases.notes: Cross-problem skill recall should expose whether the HashMap complement skill can transfer to last_seen style string work.
limitations: Only three problems exist in v1, so cross-pattern coverage is thin; current tag matching may miss this expected fact.

cases.userQuestion: Review this Search Insert attempt: should resolved binary-search confusion still appear in focused review memory?
cases.notes: Review profile excludes resolved and contradicted facts; this should be a clean stale-suppression case.
limitations: Expected facts are empty by design.

cases.userQuestion: Recall my memory about Python dict.get, key membership, and Two Sum.
cases.notes: Recall-tool profile does not include unresolved_confusion, so this is an episode-focused query.
limitations: This documents a profile limitation rather than treating python_dict_get as expected fact recall.
V1 has 12 agent-drafted queries, below the Task3.2 suggested >=30 human-reviewed query set.
Some queries intentionally expose known retrieval limitations and may score poorly in the baseline.
V1 covers five user-intent buckets; low_confidence_suppression is not covered because Task3A v1 has no low-confidence fact.
